summary.good: Air quality is satisfactory and poses little or no health risk.
summary.moderate: Air quality is acceptable. Very sensitive individuals should observe symptoms.
summary.unhealthy_sensitive: Sensitive groups (asthma, children, seniors) may experience irritation.
summary.unhealthy: Everyone may begin to experience health effects; sensitive groups more seriously.
summary.very_unhealthy: Health alert: serious risk of harm for entire population. Remain indoors.
summary.hazardous: Health emergency: life-threatening conditions for all residents.

advice.good: Air quality is clean. Ideal time for outdoor exercise, runs, and window ventilation.
advice.moderate: Acceptable air quality. Unusually sensitive people should consider limiting heavy exertion.
advice.unhealthy_sensitive: Sensitive individuals should wear an N95 mask outdoors and limit prolonged workouts.
advice.unhealthy: Avoid strenuous outdoor exertion. Close windows facing traffic and run HEPA air purifiers.
advice.very_unhealthy: Stay strictly indoors. Seal room drafts and operate continuous HEPA filtration.
advice.hazardous: Emergency condition. Remain strictly inside. Avoid all outdoor physical activity.

advisor.title: Personalized Health Advisor

activity.title: Daily Activity & Airway Protection
activity.noWindow: Check live atmospheric readings above to time errands.

low.general: Clean air conditions. Minimal to no health risk detected for the general population.
low.child: Ideal conditions for children to play, learn, and engage in outdoor sports.
low.elderly: Safe and pristine atmospheric quality for seniors and elderly walks.
low.runner: Optimal lung capacity conditions for high-intensity distance running and endurance training.
low.asthma_sensitive: Clear atmospheric conditions with very low respiratory triggers.

moderate.general: Air quality is acceptable. Very small risk for unusually sensitive individuals.
moderate.child: Generally safe, but monitor children with asthma or persistent cough during prolonged outdoor play.
moderate.elderly: Moderate air quality. Seniors with cardiovascular issues should pace outdoor strolls.
moderate.runner: Acceptable for training, but consider morning or shaded routes away from dense traffic corridors.
moderate.asthma_sensitive: Mild airborne irritants present. Keep quick-relief inhaler handy during outdoor commutes.

high.general: Elevated particulate pollution. Sensitive groups experience irritation; everyone feels mild symptoms.
high.child: Unhealthy air for young lungs. Recess and sports practices should be moved indoors.
high.elderly: Increased cardiac and respiratory burden. Limit outdoor errands and stay in air-filtered spaces.
high.runner: Strenuous aerobic exertion forces fine PM2.5 deep into alveoli. Shift workout indoors.
high.asthma_sensitive: Significant bronchospasm trigger. Avoid outdoor exposure; keep rescue medications accessible.

very_high.general: Severe pollution alert. Serious health risks for the entire populace. Avoid outdoor exposure.
very_high.child: Hazardous conditions for children. Keep strictly indoors with windows sealed and air filtered.
very_high.elderly: Life-threatening strain on cardiopulmonary systems. Remain strictly in filtered indoor environments.
very_high.runner: Dangerous airborne toxicity. Absolutely no outdoor workouts, cycling, or running.
very_high.asthma_sensitive: Critical respiratory emergency level. Stay inside sealed rooms; seek medical care if distress occurs.

low.general: Excellent conditions for all outdoor workouts, runs, and recreational sports.
low.runner: Prime conditions for marathon training, sprints, and interval workouts.
low.sensitive: Outdoor activities and gentle play are safe and highly encouraged.

moderate.general: Outdoor exercise is fine for most. Take normal hydration breaks.
moderate.runner: Safe for regular runs. If sensitive, schedule during cleanest forecast hours.
moderate.sensitive: Reduce duration of strenuous outdoor games or sports if coughing develops.

high.general: Avoid prolonged or heavy exertion outdoors. Consider gym workouts.
high.runner: Skip outdoor running. Deep breathing multiplies particulate inhalation 5-10x. Train indoors.
high.sensitive: Cease all outdoor physical activities. Remain in well-filtered indoor environments.

very_high.general: Avoid all outdoor physical activity. Keep physical strain minimal even indoors.
very_high.runner: No outdoor exercise permitted. High risk of acute pulmonary irritation.
very_high.sensitive: Strict indoor confinement. Avoid any physical exertion that increases breathing rate.

mask.none: No respirator or mask needed. Ambient air poses no particulate hazard.
mask.optionalSensitive: Standard masks are optional; sensitive individuals may prefer an N95 near congested roads.
mask.recommendedN95: Well-fitted N95 / FFP2 respirator recommended outdoors. Note: surgical and cloth masks do NOT filter fine PM2.5.
mask.criticalN95: Strict N95 / FFP2 / KN95 respirator required for any brief outdoor transit. Ensure airtight nasal seal. Note: masks cannot filter toxic gases (ozone, NO2).

ventilation.openWide: Open windows wide for fresh air exchange and natural cross-breeze ventilation.
ventilation.moderate: Natural ventilation is acceptable during daytime. Close windows if near heavy traffic intersections.
ventilation.limited: Keep windows closed during peak hours. Use recirculating air conditioning or filtered intake.
ventilation.closed: Keep all windows, doors, and drafts tightly sealed. Run continuous HEPA filtration units indoors.

bestWindow.safe: Optimal outdoor window between {start} and {end} (projected AQI ~{avgAqi}). Plan errands then.
bestWindow.unsafe: No safe continuous window found in the next 24 hours. Keep outdoor outings strictly brief.

general.low: Enjoy regular daily routines and outdoor activities without restriction.
general.moderate: Unusually sensitive people should take more breaks during intense outdoor labor.
general.high: Cut down on high-energy outdoor activities. Take frequent rests indoors.
general.very_high: Stay indoors as much as possible. Postpone non-essential travel and outdoor commitments.

child.low: Children can play freely outdoors. Natural air quality supports healthy lung development.
child.moderate: Watch for complaints of eye stinging, sneezing, or mild coughing during sports.
child.high: Move school sports, recess, and playground visits indoors. Keep windows closed at school.
child.very_high: Keep children inside air-conditioned or air-purified rooms. Seek prompt care for breathing difficulty.

elderly.low: Great weather for outdoor strolls, gardening, and socialization.
elderly.moderate: Take regular seated rests during outdoor walks. Stay hydrated.
elderly.high: Avoid exertion outdoors. Individuals with heart disease or COPD should remain inside.
elderly.very_high: Stay indoors with doors sealed. Monitor oxygen saturation and pulse if advised by your physician.

runner.low: Optimal VO2 max conditions. Ideal for long-distance tempo runs and high-aerobic workouts.
runner.moderate: Good for training. Monitor midday ozone levels; choose early morning trails.
runner.high: Aerobic respiration dramatically increases toxic particulate intake. Switch to indoor treadmill or gym.
runner.very_high: Danger of acute bronchitis or lung inflammation. Completely cancel outdoor endurance workouts.

asthma_sensitive.low: Clean air. Low trigger risk for bronchospasm. Safe for normal outdoor routines.
asthma_sensitive.moderate: Keep prescribed bronchodilator/inhaler with you at all times when outdoors.
asthma_sensitive.high: High trigger risk for asthma flare-ups. Stay in sealed room with HEPA air cleaner. Follow your action plan.
asthma_sensitive.very_high: Severe bronchospasm hazard. Avoid any outdoor exposure. Seek medical attention immediately for wheezing.

purifier.title: HEPA Air Filtration
purifier.low: Indoor air quality is generally good. Standard airflow or low purifier setting is sufficient.
purifier.high: Run true-HEPA air cleaners continuously on high. Clean pre-filters and seal doors.

activity.title: Exertion Management
activity.low: Normal exertion is safe for all age groups.
activity.moderate: Pace strenuous workouts and stay hydrated.
activity.high: Scale back strenuous cardio. Move physical training into filtered indoor spaces.
activity.very_high: Absolute cessation of strenuous physical activities outdoors.

ventilation.title: Indoor Ventilation & Windows
ventilation.low: Allow fresh air to circulate freely through home and office windows.
ventilation.high: Seal windows, balconies, and exterior exhaust dampers against outdoor smog ingress.

mask.title: Respirator Protocol
mask.high: Wear a certified N95/FFP2 respirator with tight perimeter seal. Cloth masks are ineffective for PM2.5.

hydration.title: Airway Hydration
hydration.desc: Drink water frequently. Hydrated mucous membranes help airway cilia expel trapped airborne particles.

medical.title: Respiratory Action Plan
medical.general: Keep basic first-aid and saline nasal rinses available if experiencing throat or eye irritation.
medical.asthma: Keep rescue inhalers accessible. Have your personalized asthma action plan ready and follow medication regimens.

disclaimer.notice: General guidance only: Health advice in Vayu is for wellness awareness and educational reference. It does not constitute medical diagnosis, clinical prescription, or formal healthcare recommendations. Always consult a qualified medical professional for health concerns.

emergency.title: Urgent Medical Notice
emergency.alert: Urgent Medical Alert: Atmospheric pollution is dangerously high. If you or someone with you experiences severe shortness of breath, continuous coughing, wheezing, or chest tightness, seek immediate emergency medical care.
